requirements.requirement: Limit traffic from node2 toward node3 to 1 Mbit/s
requirements.summary: VyOS HTB shaper policy (bandwidth/ceiling 1mbit) applied as egress on node1's node3-facing interface (eth2), confirmed via 'tc class show' showing rate/ceil 1Mbit, and directly validated with iperf3 showing node2->node3 throughput dropping from ~21.7 Gbit/s baseline to ~1.13 Mbit/s after shaping, and ~1.27 Mbit/s after all three nodes were rebooted, confirming persistence.

requirements.requirement: Leave traffic from node3 toward node2 unrestricted
requirements.summary: iperf3 measurements in the reverse direction after shaping was applied showed ~1.54 Gbit/s (vs ~21.6 Gbit/s baseline, consistent with normal iperf3 variance/no artificial cap), and ~1.17 Gbit/s after the restart cycle, confirming the shaper did not restrict node3->node2 traffic.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 communicate through node1 across their separate private networks (topology prerequisite for directional shaping to be meaningful)
requirements.summary: Static addressing was assigned on node1's eth1/eth2 (10.10.12.1, 10.10.13.1) and on node2/node3's eth1 interfaces with static routes via node1, and a ping from node2 to node3 showed TTL=63 (one hop lower than a direct TTL=64), confirming traffic transits node1 rather than a flat shared network.

overall_summary: The executor correctly discovered the real topology (node1 with two private-facing NICs to node2 and node3), configured static addressing/routing so traffic transits node1, applied a VyOS HTB QoS shaper limiting node2->node3 to 1 Mbit/s on node1's node3-facing egress interface while leaving node3->node2 unshaped, and directly validated the asymmetric behavior with iperf3 both before and after applying the shaper. All three nodes were then rebooted with clear boot-id evidence of restart and post-restart confirmation that addressing, routing, firewall zones, the QoS shaper, and the required 1 Mbit/s asymmetric throughput all persisted. Hygiene is good overall with a few bounded, mostly-reverted diagnostic mutations and some leftover log files as minor residue.
limitations: Reverse-direction (node3->node2) 'unrestricted' throughput after shaping (~1.5 Gbit/s and ~1.17 Gbit/s) is noticeably lower than the pre-shaping baseline (~21.6 Gbit/s) in both runs, which is consistent with normal iperf3/virtual-NIC variance and TCP retransmit noise (retr counts visible in the traces) rather than evidence of an unintended cap, but the trace does not include a definitive isolation of that variance.

Firewalld zone changes moved eth1 on node2/node3 from 'public' to 'trusted', which is a broad permissive zone; this was necessary to unblock forwarded traffic but was not scoped to a minimal rule, a hygiene tradeoff rather than a task-outcome issue.
Diagnostic log files left in /tmp on node2/node3 were not cleaned up after troubleshooting, though this is low-severity residue.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were either necessary prerequisites (static addressing/routing, firewalld zone changes required to unblock the private-link traffic that public zone's REJECT rule was blocking, iperf3 installation for verification, the QoS shaper itself) or bounded final-evidence collection (iperf3 tests, reboots). A few unnecessary/diagnostic mutations occurred during troubleshooting: a temporary python http.server was started on node3 (cmd-1e851ad012c94b92) purely to debug connectivity and was later killed (cmd-148209f54b774e9f), a loopback iperf3 self-test was run on node2 (cmd-03bcec85af9e41be) that had no bearing on the final solution, and an initial nmcli route configuration on node2/node3 mistakenly set a gateway that produced a duplicate default route (cmd-d9020ba59781448d, cmd-463737bf6dd14d4b), which was promptly corrected (cmd-d5e46328126849b7, cmd-2cd1e75f7b0f4c32) — a legitimate corrective action, not penalized. Minor residue remains: diagnostic log files (iperf_srv*.log, loopsrv.log, http.log, reboot.log, iperf3_install.log) were left in /tmp on node2 and node3, and the firewalld zone for eth1 was broadened to 'trusted' (unrestricted) rather than a narrower custom rule, which is a reasonable but somewhat permissive choice on an isolated private link. Post-restart package-health and failed-services checks show no damaged state on any node.
